hints: Remember that sodium and sodium hydroxide do not react with exactly the same functional groups, so focus on which groups each reagent can deprotonate.
A charge of -1 with NaOH(aq) tells you J must contain just one carboxylic acid group, $-CO_2H$.
To reach a total charge of -3 with Na, count how many extra alcohol $-OH$ groups must be present alongside that one acid group.
walkthrough:
**Recall what Na reacts with**

Sodium metal is a very strong base. It reacts with all acidic protons in alcohols and carboxylic acids.

Each $-OH$ and each $-CO_2H$ loses $H^+$ to form $-O^-$ and $-CO_2^-$:
$$R-OH + Na \rightarrow R-O^-Na^+ + \frac{1}{2}H_2$$

**Recall what NaOH(aq) reacts with**

Dilute aqueous NaOH is a weaker base. It neutralises carboxylic acids but it does NOT deprotonate simple alcohols.

$$R-CO_2H + NaOH \rightarrow R-CO_2^-Na^+ + H_2O$$

**Use the charges to count groups**

With excess NaOH, J gives a -1 ion. So J must have one $-CO_2H$ group.

With excess Na, J gives a -3 ion. So J must have 3 acidic H atoms in total.

**Deduce the structure of J**

One of those 3 acidic H atoms is from the one $-CO_2H$. The other two must come from two alcohol $-OH$ groups.

So J = 1 carboxylic acid + 2 alcohols. Only $HOCH_2CH(OH)CH_2CO_2H$ fits this.

options.A: Contains two alcohol groups ($HOCH_2-$ and $-CH(OH)-$) plus one carboxylic acid ($-CO_2H$). Na removes all 3 protons to give a -3 ion, while NaOH removes only the carboxylic proton to give a -1 ion. This matches both observations perfectly.
options.B: Contains one $-CO_2H$, one alcohol $-OH$, and one aldehyde $-CHO$. Aldehydes do not react with Na or NaOH to give ions. So Na would give a -2 ion, not -3. Students choosing this forget to check that $-CHO$ is not acidic.
options.C: Contains two $-CO_2H$ groups and one alcohol $-OH$. Na would indeed give -3, but NaOH would neutralise both acids to give a -2 ion, not -1. This is the trap for students who only check the sodium result.
options.D: Contains one alcohol $-OH$, one ketone $-CO-$, and one aldehyde $-CHO$. Only the alcohol reacts with Na to give -1, and nothing reacts with NaOH to give an organic ion. Students choosing this confuse carbonyl groups with acidic groups.
